speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this chronic cough and shortness of breath, and does it worsen at night or with exercise?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for over six months, and it gets much worse at night. It also makes me feel quite short of breath when I try to exercise or do my delivery work. However, the integrated care record from another facility shows confirmed asthma. There is no need to re-examine. Please accept and proceed.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the record mentions asthma, but given the severity of your shortness of breath during work, I need to confirm if you have ever experienced wheezing or if your symptoms improve with a rescue inhaler. REQUEST TEST: Spirometry with bronchodilator response.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising given your history; since your spirometry is normal, have you noticed any specific triggers like dust, chemicals, or cold air that worsen your symptoms? Also, do you have any history of acid reflux or heartburn?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've noticed that the cough gets significantly worse when I'm driving and exposed to exhaust fumes or dust. I also sometimes get heartburn, especially after eating large meals or lying down to sleep. I want to emphasize that, the integrated care record from another facility shows confirmed asthma. There is no need to re-examine. Please accept and proceed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal spirometry, your symptoms worsening with exhaust fumes, and the presence of heartburn, I suspect this may be cough-variant asthma triggered by irritants or gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). REQUEST TEST: 24-hour pH monitoring and FeNO (Fractional exhaled Nitric Oxide).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: 24-hour pH monitoring: Abnormal (elevated acid exposure time); FeNO: Elevated (45 ppb)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cough-Variant Asthma with comorbid Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).
